t:
The funds that, on the day before the transfer date, the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision (in consultation with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Chairperson of the Corporation, and the Chairman of the Board of Governors) determines are not necessary to dispose of the affairs of the Office of Thrift Supervision under section 325 and are available to the Office of Thrift Supervision to pay the expenses of the Office of Thrift Supervision—
    (1) relating to the functions of the Office of Thrift Supervision transferred under section 312(b)(2)(B), shall be transferred to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on the transfer date; 
    (2) relating to the functions of the Office of Thrift Supervision transferred under section 312(b)(2)(C), shall be transferred to the Corporation on the transfer date; and 
    (3) relating to the functions of the Office of Thrift Supervision transferred under section 312(b)(1)(A), shall be transferred to the Board of Governors on the transfer date.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the phrase "in consultation with" signals participation. However, the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision consults only the Comptroller of the Currency, the FDIC Chairperson, and the Chairman of the Federal Reserve Board, all of whom are federal officials. This is purely intra-government coordination over a transfer of funds between federal agencies, with no state, tribal, private, or public party involved.
fable.s: in consultation with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Chairperson of the Corporation, and the Chairman of the Board of Governors

opus.w: The only consultation here is between federal officials: the OTS Director, the Comptroller of the Currency, the FDIC Chairperson and the Federal Reserve Board Chairman. No one outside the federal government takes part in the decision. Consultation among agencies inside the government is not participation, so the word "consultation" does not make this a "Yes."
opus.s: the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision (in consultation with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Chairperson of the Corporation, and the Chairman of the Board of Governors) determines are not necessary
opus.b: The tempting reading is to call this "Yes" because of the phrase "in consultation with." That fails because every official consulted (the Comptroller of the Currency, the FDIC Chairperson and the Federal Reserve Board Chairman) works inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The consultation described is between federal officials and heads of federal agencies (OTS, OCC, RTC, and Federal Reserve). Since all actors involved are inside the federal government, this constitutes intra-governmental coordination rather than participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes consultation between federal agencies or officials.
qwen_chat.s: the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision (in consultation with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Chairperson of the Corporation, and the Chairman of the Board of Governors) determines
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The phrase "in consultation with" suggests participation. However, the parties involved—the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision, the Comptroller of the Currency, the Chairperson of the Corporation (Resolution Trust Corporation), and the Chairman of the Board of Governors (Federal Reserve)—are all federal officials or heads of federal agencies. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
